Decision: Added (authorized — 'add narrowly scoped test-build-only hooks only when strictly required to invoke an existing production control path')
Rationale: The renderer's exposed liveMemoryFreezeStart preload call sends the pre-Batch-B1.1 payload shape while the real IPC handler now requires {proposalId, consentToken} — a real, pre-existing gap in the shipped renderer/preload wiring (not introduced by any gate in this engagement). This hook is gated on SOLITH_TEST_BUILD='1' (identical throw-guard pattern to every existing Gate 2.1 hook), reachable only via globalThis (electronApp.evaluate), never exposed via IPC/contextBridge, and calls the EXACT SAME production functions (LiveMemorySession.proposeFreeze, requestPrivilegedWriteConsent — which still respects SOLITH_PRIVILEGED_CONSENT and enforces real consent/identity checks — and MemoryManager.freezeStart) that the real (currently broken) IPC flow would call. It does not fabricate a result, bypass feature-flag/identity/consent enforcement, or expose an arbitrary PID/address/command interface — it takes the same senderId/address/dataType/value/intervalMs parameters a real propose-freeze call would take.

Item: Freeze-tick timing (initial wait bumped from ~700-800ms to 2.5-6s)
Decision: Adjusted test-only timing, no production change
Rationale: Per-tick identity re-verification (verifyAttachedProcessIdentity, which computes a real executable SHA256 via a subprocess on Windows) is substantially slower than the freeze interval itself — the same class of timing issue documented in Gate 2.2A's evidence. Not a production defect; the tests were under-waiting.

Item: Only harness-created SOLITH and fixture processes were terminated
Rationale: Every process.kill() call in the new test file targets either the harness's own spawned Gate2_2Fixture.exe or ctx.app.process().pid (the harness's own launched Solith.exe instance for Phase 4.6's forced-termination scenario). No unrelated process was targeted.

The new hook adds reachability, not a bypass: it still calls proposeFreeze (which performs no authorization itself, matching the real propose handler), still calls verifyAttachedProcessIdentity and getAttachedIdentity (fails closed identically to the real handler), and still calls requestPrivilegedWriteConsent with a real consent binding (only auto-approved via the PRE-EXISTING SOLITH_PRIVILEGED_CONSENT test/headless env var, not a new bypass) before calling the real manager.freezeStart, which itself re-validates the consent token via consumeWriteConsent.
